items.title: Quiver full-flag incidence has a smooth projective compactification
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the relative Proj, projectivity and scheme-properness suppliers ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[thm-projective-morphism-proper]]); the adapted-basis and chart selections are made on fixed finite-dimensional data, so the lemma introduces no further choice.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the relative Proj and scheme-properness suppliers. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite loopless quiver, with arbitrary finitely many arrows between two distinct vertices. Let $V= igoplus_iV_i$ be a finite-dimensional complex graded vector space, $ eta_i=\dim V_i$, $E_V= igoplus_{h:i	o j}\operatorname{Hom}(V_i,V_j)$ and $G_V=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$. Let $
u=(
u_1,\ldots,
u_m)$ be a word with $ eta_i$ occurrences of $i$. Let $\mathcal F_
u$ be the variety of increasing full graded flags $0=F^0\subset F^1\subset\cdots\subset F^m=V$ with $F^r/F^{r-1}$ of color $
u_r$. Then $X_
u=\{(x,F):x_hF_i^r\subset F_j^r	ext{ for all }h:i	o j,r\}$ is a $G_V$-equivariant vector subbundle $W_
u$ of $E_V	imes\mathcal F_
u$. Its rank is $\sum_{h:i	o j}\#\{(p,q):
u_p=i,
u_q=j,q<p\}$ and its dimension is that rank plus $\sum_i eta_i( eta_i-1)/2$. The map $\pi_
u:X_
u	o E_V$ is projective.

Put $\mathbb P_{m lines}(U)=\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{Sym}(U^\vee)$. Then the bundle inclusion defines a $G_V$-equivariant projective map $ ar\pi_
u:\mathbb P_{m lines}(W_
u\oplus\mathcal O)	o\mathbb P_{m lines}(E_V\oplus\mathbb C)$ whose source is smooth projective and whose restriction over the affine chart $t
e0$ is exactly $\pi_
u$. The analogous associated-bundle construction over any finite product of complex Grassmannians formed from tautological bundles is a projective map between smooth projective varieties, restricting over its affine chart to the associated incidence map.
items.strategy:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Varagnolo-Vasserot, Canonical bases and KLR-algebras, arXiv:0901.3992v2, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 3-4): the representation space $E_V$, the group $G_V$, the flag variety of type $y$, the variety of $x$-stable flags and its proper first projection; Bozec, Quivers with loops and perverse sheaves, arXiv:1401.5302v4, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 2-3): the same construction with increasing flags and the proper map $\pi_{i,a}$; Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Secs. 6.m-6.n (printed pp. 149-152): Plucker realization of Grassmannians, the complementary-subspace charts, and the flag variety as a closed subset of a product of Grassmannians. [F1] [[def-projective-bundle-scheme]]: $\mathbb P_S(E)=\operatorname{Proj}_S\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ in the quotient convention, with $\mathbb P_S(E)	imes_SU\cong\mathbb P^{r-1}_U$ over a frame $E|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$ and its homogeneous-coordinate charts; the rank-zero case is the empty scheme, which is why the trivial line summand $\mathcal O$ is adjoined. [F2] [[lem-grassmannian-standard-affine-charts]]: the standard graph charts of $\operatorname{Gr}(d,V)$ are affine spaces of dimension $d(\dim V-d)$ with regular transitions, covering the Grassmannian, including the rank-zero and top-degree points. [F3] [[thm-plucker-image-closed]]: the Plucker map is injective with closed image cut out by the Plucker relations, so Grassmannians are projective. [F4] [[cor-projective-variety-product-exists]]: the product of nonempty projective varieties is realized as their Segre image and is a projective variety. [F5] [[thm-projective-morphism-proper]]: under AC every projective morphism is proper. Step 1.1. Forgetting repeated colors identifies $\mathcal F_
u$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Flag}(V_i)$; the full flag variety of $V_i$ is the closed incidence locus of successive inclusions of tautological subspaces in $\prod_{d=1}^{ eta_i-1}\operatorname{Gr}(d,V_i)$, hence projective by [F2], [F3], [F4], and each successive map choosing a line in the next quotient is locally a projective-space bundle of relative dimensions $ eta_i-1,\dots,1$ by [F1], so the total space is smooth of dimension $ eta_i( eta_i-1)/2$; the graph charts of [F2] give algebraic local bases adapted to the tautological flag. Empty products and $ eta_i\in\{0,1\}$ give points. Step 2.1. On such an adapted-basis chart label each basis vector $e_p$ by its position $p$ in $
u$. The condition $x_hF^r_i\subset F^r_j$ says the coefficient of $e_q$ in $x_he_p$ vanishes whenever $q>p$; looplessness makes $q=p$ impossible, so the free coefficients are exactly the pairs with $
u_p=i$, $
u_q=j$, $q<p$, in the number stated, and the defining equations are homogeneous linear in the representation coordinates. Changes of adapted basis preserve stability and act linearly on these free coordinates, so the local kernels glue to a vector subbundle $W_
u\subset E_V	imes\mathcal F_
u$ with locally free quotient, of smooth total space and the stated dimension; the action of $g\in G_V$ on matrices and flags preserves the incidence equations. Step 3.1. Intrinsically $X_
u$ is the common zero locus of the maps $x_h:F^r_i	o V_j/F^r_j$, hence closed in $E_V	imes\mathcal F_
u$; the projection $E_V	imes\mathcal F_
u	o E_V$ is projective because $\mathcal F_
u$ is projective over the point by step 1.1, so $\pi_
u$ is projective and, by [F5], proper. No paving or semismallness hypothesis enters. Step 3.2. The inclusion $W_
u\oplus\mathcal O\hookrightarrow(E_V\oplus\mathbb C)	imes\mathcal F_
u$ induces a closed immersion $\mathbb P_{m lines}(W_
u\oplus\mathcal O)\hookrightarrow\mathbb P_{m lines}(E_V\oplus\mathbb C)	imes\mathcal F_
u$: on a local bundle chart the equations are the same homogeneous linear equations with the extra coordinate $t$ unconstrained. Projection gives the $G_V$-equivariant projective map $ ar\pi_
u$, whose source is smooth by [F1] and step 1.1; over $t
e0$ the unique representative $(w,1)$ identifies the inverse image with $X_
u$ scheme-theoretically. Step 3.3. For the finite associated version put $B_N=\prod_{ eta_i>0}\operatorname{Gr}( eta_i,N_i)$ with tautological bundles $S_i$, and let $\mathcal F_{
u,N}$ parametrize chains inside each $S_i$, recording also the terminal $ eta_i$-plane in $\mathbb C^{N_i}$; the chart and incidence arguments of steps 1.1-2.1 apply verbatim to give the associated incidence vector subbundle $W_{
u,N}$ of the pullback of $E_N= igoplus_{h:i	o j}\operatorname{Hom}(S_i,S_j)$, omitting zero-rank terms. Step 4.1. Absolute projectivity of the target needs no general compactification theorem: with $D= igotimes_{ eta_i>0}\det S_i$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}(S_i,S_j)\otimes D\cong igwedge^{ eta_i-1}S_i\otimes S_j\otimes igotimes_{l
e i}\det S_l$ using $S_i^\vee\otimes\det S_i= igwedge^{ eta_i-1}S_i$; exterior powers of tautological subbundles embed in exterior powers of the trivial bundle, so $(E_N\oplus\mathcal O)\otimes D$ embeds in a finite trivial bundle with locally free quotient, and tensoring lines by $D$ identifies $\mathbb P_{m lines}((E_N\oplus\mathcal O)\otimes D)\cong\mathbb P_{m lines}(E_N\oplus\mathcal O)$, a closed subvariety of $B_N	imes\mathbb P^M$, smooth and projective by [F1], [F2], [F3]. Step 5.1. The incidence inclusion embeds $\mathbb P_{m lines}(W_{
u,N}\oplus\mathcal O)$ closed in $\mathbb P_{m lines}(E_N\oplus\mathcal O)	imes_{B_N}\mathcal F_{
u,N}$; the fiber product is closed in the product of the projective varieties, being the inverse image of the closed diagonal, so the source and the induced map are projective, and over $t
e0$ the inverse image is the associated incidence by the same unique-representative argument. Empty dimension, zero arrows and arbitrary finite multiplicities are included. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3, step 4.1]

references.title: M. Varagnolo, E. Vasserot, Canonical bases and KLR-algebras, arXiv:0901.3992v2, Sec. 1.1
T. Bozec, Quivers with loops and perverse sheaves, arXiv:1401.5302v4, Sec. 1.1
J. S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Secs. 6.m-6.n

items.title: Full quiver-flag pushforwards are semisimple in characteristic zero
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the geometry supplier [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]], the finite triangulation supplier [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]] and the equivariant constructible-category suppliers of [[equivariant-constructible-perverse-foundations]]; the proof makes only finite selections of words, frame dimensions and idempotents already provided by those items.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the geometry and equivariant constructible-category suppliers. Let $\Gamma$ be any finite loopless complex quiver, with arbitrary finite arrow multiplicities, and let $ eta$ be any finite dimension vector. For a color word $
u$ of content $ eta$, use the increasing full graded flag incidence $\pi_
u:X_
u	o E_V$ and $G_V=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$ of [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]]. For every coefficient field $k$ of characteristic zero, in the actual bounded equivariant constructible category,
$$L_
u=R\pi_{
u!}k_{X_
u}[d_
u],\qquad d_
u=\dim_\mathbb C X_
u,$$
is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple $G_V$-equivariant perverse sheaves. Consequently the finite sum over all such words is a semisimple complex in the same sense. No semismallness, finite-ADE hypothesis or affine paving of the fibers of $\pi_
u$ is required.
items.strategy:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Varagnolo-Vasserot, arXiv:0901.3992v2, Secs. 1.2-1.3 (PDF pp. 4-6): $D_G(X)$ is the bounded derived category of simplicial sheaves on the action nerve whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian, perversity is detected on $X$, and (1.5) the complexes $L_y=(\pi_y)_!(k)$, $L_y^\vee=L_y[2d_y]$, $\delta L_y=L_y[d_y]$ are semisimple in $D_{G_V}(E_V)$; Bozec, arXiv:1401.5302v4, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 2-3): for the increasing flag variety the first projection is proper and $\pi_{i,a!}1$ is semisimple by the BBD decomposition theorem; Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, Asterisque 100, Theoreme 6.2.5 with 6.2.7 (PDF pp. 161-163): a proper direct image of a semisimple geometrically-origin complex is semisimple; Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Secs. 6.m-6.n (printed pp. 149-152): the flag and Grassmannian models used by the finite frame constructions. [F1] [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]] gives the $G_V$-equivariant smooth incidence $X_
u	o E_V$ with its explicit smooth projective compactifications $ ar X_{
u,N}	o ar E_N$ restricting to $\pi_{
u,N}$ over $t
e0$, and [[thm-projective-pushforward-of-smooth-constant-sheaves-has-semisimple-perverse-cohomology]] is the compact smooth-source projective theorem over every characteristic-zero coefficient field. [F2] [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] supplies the ambient category $D^b_{G,c}(E_V;k)$ of the claim; [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] supplies the finite-resolution functors $Q_N$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{E_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$ for $m\le b+r_N-a$ on amplitudes $[b,a]$, retract closure and the degree-zero ring comparison; [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] supplies the resolution-triple model and idempotent completeness of the category; [[lem-general-linear-stiefel-perverse-normalization-is-exact-and-conservative]] makes $Q_N(-)[s_N]$ perverse exact and conservative and preserves and reflects perverse concentration and simplicity at the stabilization bound. [F3] [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] computes $Q_N$ on pushforwards by equivariant proper base change, and [[thm-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] identifies the equivariant perverse heart and its simple objects. [F4] [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] supplies the ordinary perverse t-structure on the finite models, open restriction perverse exactness and the description of simple objects as $IC_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$; the standard consequence $j^*IC_Z(L)=IC_{Z\cap U}(L|_{Z^{sm}\cap U})$ for an open immersion $j:U	o Y$ follows from the intermediate-extension description as the image of ${}^pH^0j_!L	o{}^pH^0Rj_*L$ together with open base change. [F5] [[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]]: a nonempty Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety has surjective fundamental-group map. [F6] [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]] bounds the cohomology of a complex algebraic variety of dimension $f$ by $[0,2f]$ through finite real-dimensional cochain models. Step 1.1. There are finitely many color words $
u$ of content $ eta$; put $K= igoplus_
u L_
u$ and $f=\sum_i eta_i( eta_i-1)/2$. A fiber of $\pi_
u$ is a closed subvariety of the color flag variety of dimension $f$, so by [F6] its constructible cohomology lies in degrees $[0,2f]$; proper base change gives ordinary amplitude $[-d_
u,2f-d_
u]$ for $L_
u$, so $K$ has amplitude $[b,a]$ with $b=-\max_
u d_
u$ and $a=2f-\min_
u d_
u$. Choose $N_i\ge eta_i+1$ with $r_N=2\min_{ eta_i>0}(N_i- eta_i)\ge a-b=2f+\max_
u d_
u-\min_
u d_
u$; for the trivial group the identity model has $r_N=\infty$. [F1, F2, F6, construct] Step 2.1. In the finite model $E_N$ one has $Q_N(K)[s_N]= igoplus_
u R\pi_{
u,N!}k_{X_{
u,N}}[d_
u+s_N]$ by [F3], with $\dim_\mathbb C X_{
u,N}=d_
u+s_N$ and $s_N=\dim_\mathbb C B_N$ by [F1]. Each $\pi_{
u,N}$ is the $t
e0$ restriction of the projective map $ ar\pi_{
u,N}$ between smooth projective varieties of the same source dimension, so applying the compact smooth-source semisimplicity theorem [F1] to each $ ar\pi_{
u,N}$ and then ordinary open base change expresses each summand of $Q_N(K)[s_N]$ as a finite sum of shifts of simple ordinary perverse sheaves on $E_N$. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct] Step 3.1. Each such simple summand is $S=IC_Z(L)$ for an irreducible support $Z\subset ar E_N$ and a simple local system $L$ on a dense smooth open $Z^{sm}\subset Z$. If $Z\cap E_N=\varnothing$ its restriction is zero; otherwise $Z\cap E_N$ is a nonempty dense open of $Z$. Restriction along $E_N\hookrightarrow ar E_N$ is perverse exact, and $j^*IC_Z(L)=IC_{Z\cap E_N}(L|_{Z^{sm}\cap E_N})$ by [F4]. The inclusion $Z^{sm}\cap E_N\hookrightarrow Z^{sm}$ is a nonempty Zariski open of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety, so [F5] makes the fundamental-group map surjective, and a simple representation stays simple after restriction along a surjection; hence the restricted local system is simple and its intermediate extension is a simple ordinary perverse sheaf. Therefore $Q_N(K)[s_N]$, and likewise each $Q_N(L_
u)[s_N]$, is a finite sum of shifts of simple ordinary perverse sheaves on $E_N$. [F4, F5, step 2.1, construct] Step 4.1. A finite decomposition into shifts of simples determines mutually orthogonal idempotent endomorphisms of $K_N$ with sum the identity. The amplitude bound of step 1.1 gives the degree-zero ring comparison $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}(K_N)$ from [F2], so all idempotents lift uniquely and simultaneously with their relations; the lifted idempotents split in the idempotent-complete actual equivariant category by [F2], producing $G_V$-equivariant direct summands of $K$ whose finite models are exactly the summands of step 3.1. [F2, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] Step 5.1. Let $T$ be a lifted summand whose model after the common shift is a shift of a simple perverse sheaf. Perverse exactness and conservativity of $Q_N(-)[s_N]$ [F2] force $T=U[j]$ for perverse $U$; a nonzero proper perverse subobject of $U$ would be carried by the exact conservative functor to a nonzero proper subobject of the simple model, so $U$ is simple equivariantly. [F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] Step 6.1. Only the finite set of words, one sufficiently large frame model and the actual degree-zero Hom bound were used; applying the argument to $K$ proves the sum clause and applying it to a single $L_
u$ proves the individual clause. All multiplicities and dimensions enter through the rank, the flag dimension $f$ and the compactification of [F1], and characteristic zero enters only through the compact smooth-source theorem and the scalar conventions of the equivariant category [F2]. No semismallness, finite-ADE hypothesis or affine paving of fibers is used. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 5.1]

title: Quiver Full Flag Projective Semisimplicity Examples

items.title: One-color quiver full flags need not be semismall
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the cited geometry suppliers through the incidence lemma; the rank and defect computations themselves are finite and choice-free.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Take the loopless quiver with a single vertex and no arrows, $\dim V=n\ge2$, and its unique word. Then $E_V=0$ and $X_\nu=\operatorname{Flag}(V)$. The proper incidence map to the point need not be semismall: in this example its defect $2\dim(\text{fiber})+\dim(\text{image})-\dim X_\nu$ is positive.
items.strategy:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Sources: Varagnolo-Vasserot, arXiv:0901.3992v2, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 3-4) and Bozec, arXiv:1401.5302v4, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 2-3) for the incidence model and the rank bookkeeping of the empty-arrow case; Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Secs. 6.m-6.n (printed pp. 149-152) for the flag-variety model. Step 1.1. The incidence lemma [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]] gives rank zero and $\dim X_
u=n(n-1)/2$, and all of $X_
u$ is the fiber over the point $E_V=0$. [given, algebra] Step 2.1. The defect $2\dim(	ext{fiber})+\dim(	ext{image})-\dim X_
u$ is therefore $n(n-1)/2>0$ for $n\ge2$, while for $n=0$ or $n=1$ the flag space is a point and the defect is zero. Hence a general quiver-flag decomposition proof must allow the non-semismall case. [step 1.1, algebra]

items.title: Multiple-arrow incidence compactifications in dimension one at each vertex
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the cited geometry suppliers through the incidence lemma; the rank and compactification computations themselves are finite and choice-free.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Take two vertices $i,j$, $h\ge0$ arrows $i\to j$, no other arrows, and $\beta_i=\beta_j=1$. Then $E_V=\mathbb C^h$. For the increasing word $(i,j)$ the stable incidence is the point $x=0$; for the word $(j,i)$ it is all of $\mathbb C^h$.
items.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Sources: Varagnolo-Vasserot, arXiv:0901.3992v2, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 3-4) and Bozec, arXiv:1401.5302v4, Sec. 1.1 (PDF pp. 2-3) for the increasing flag convention, the incidence model and the stability rank count; Milne, Algebraic Geometry, Secs. 6.m-6.n (printed pp. 149-152) for the flag model. Step 1.1. In either word the graded flag base is a point. For $(i,j)$ the source basis vector occurs before the target, so every arrow coordinate is forbidden by stability and the vector-bundle rank is zero; for $(j,i)$ every arrow coordinate is allowed and the rank is $h$. These are the explicit rank counts of [[lem-quiver-full-flag-incidence-has-a-smooth-projective-compactification]]. [given, algebra] Step 2.1. The line-projective compactifications are respectively the point $[0:1]\subset\mathbb P^h$ and the identity $\mathbb P^h\to\mathbb P^h$, and their inverse images of $t\ne0$ are exactly the two stated affine incidence maps; $h=0$ gives two point maps. [step 1.1, algebra]
